claim: *The engineering modeling repertoire.* Familiar representations preserve different relationships for different engineering questions. Similar graphical forms can carry different semantics: an arrow may represent a dependency, transition, flow, permission, ownership relation, or derivation.

topology.description: Nine peer forms. Structural fork, state machine, data-flow chain, exclusive ownership, permission graph, quantitative comparison, entity relations, provenance convergence and call graph retain original edges.

required_terms: Q: What depends on what? P: Reachability, layering, forbidden edges A: Traversal, cycles, paths
Q: What may happen next? P: Legal states, safety, liveness A: Model checking; search
Q: Where does data flow? P: Sources, sinks, paths, transforms A: Flow, taint, dependencies
Q: Who may control what? P: Exclusivity, transfer, reclaim A: Interleavings; invariants
Q: What is permitted? P: Consistency, exclusion, implication A: Rules; constraint checks
Q: How much / what bound? P: Budget, margin, capacity, rate A: Aggregate / optimize
Q: Entities and relations? P: Keys, cardinality, references A: Joins; schema checking
Q: What produced this? P: Attribution, lineage, evidence A: Lineage / audit traversal
Q: What may call what? P: Entry points, reachable calls A: Call-graph traversal
Q = question · P = property · A = analysis
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Nine native mini-graphs retain the original edge endpoints and directions. Questions, properties and analyses use Q/P/A labels with an explicit legend, allowing 9pt annotations at native print size. Color backgrounds are removed; separators and labels identify peer forms.
alt: Nine peer panels show component dependency, finite-state transitions, data flow, ownership, permissions, quantitative bounds, entity relations, provenance, and calls. Each retains its distinct graph and lists its question, property and analysis. Crossed dashed arrows denote a stale ownership claim and a prohibited call; quantitative inputs converge on an error rate compared with a less-than-one-percent bound. Provenance shows source and transform converging on an artifact. Black lines, labels and separators distinguish all panels without color.
